newsitem.title: DJIBOUTI: Somali warlord in talks with Djibouti president.
newsitem.headline: Somali warlord in talks with Djibouti president.

text.p: Somali faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed met Djibouti President Hassan Gouled in Djibouti on Sunday for talks on reconciling warring Somali groups.

Ali Mahdi heads the United Somali Congress (USC) and Somali Salvation Alliance (SSA) group which controls the northern part of the Somali capital, Mogadishu. He arrived in Djibouti late on Saturday from Sana'a, the Yemeni capital.
Aides said Ali Mahdi, accompanied by a 13-man delegation, had discussed with Yemeni leaders the prospects for organising a Somali reconciliation conference in Yemen.

They said he was willing to hold discussions with his main Somali rival, Hussein Farah Aideed, who took over the leadership of the Somali National Alliance (SNA) after the recent death of his father, Mohamed Farah Aideed.
In an interview on Djibouti radio on Sunday, Ali Mahdi said he was confident about the possibility of reaching an agreement on the future of Somalia in the near future.
Somali sources said Yemen was trying to get Hussein Farah Aideed to support the proposed reconciliation conference.

Somalia has had no effective government since the ousting of former president Mohamed Siad Barre in January 1991. The northern half of the country -- which borders on Djibouti -- has seceded to form the self-proclaimed Somaliland Republic, with Hargeisa as its capital, while the rest of Somalia is divided between rival factions.
